us: Hegseth keeps strikes 'by no means' foreclosed · Toughest penalties held in reserve
effects: Tanker disabled near Ash Shishah · Brent ~$92 after −2% · No Chinese banks named
iran: Madanizadeh: 'enemies should wait for an attack' · IRGC threatens energy chokepoints
tldr: Hours after the economic campaign's unveiling, an oil tanker was struck by an unknown projectile and disabled 9nm northeast of Ash Shishah, Oman — crew safe, no blame assigned. Tehran promised retaliation ('our defense is no longer so defensive'), with the IRGC threatening blows to US vital interests and energy chokepoints, while China's Foreign Ministry formally rejected the sanctions even though no Chinese institutions were designated. Oil extended its decline toward $92 Brent as Pakistan's mediation round closed without a visible outcome.

events.title: Oil tanker struck by unknown projectile, disabled 9nm northeast of Ash Shishah
events.summary: UKMTO warning 120-26 reported the master of an oil tanker saying the vessel was hit by an unknown projectile, damaging the engine room and disabling it; crew safe, environmental impact unknown, authorities investigating. UKMTO assigned no blame; The War Zone called an Iranian role 'extremely likely'. The strike landed within roughly a day of Treasury's launch and OFAC's guidance telling shipping to refuse Iran's Hormuz transit demands. Hours earlier, the Houthis claimed a ballistic-missile hit on the Saudi tanker Amzan off Yanbu — their 'blockade for blockade' spillover.

events.title: Madanizadeh: 'our defense is no longer so defensive; the enemies should wait for an attack'
events.summary: The economy minister told state television Iran is 'fully prepared' and warned enemies to 'wait for an attack' after what he called an economic-terrorist threat. IRGC spokesman Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi vowed heavy blows to US vital interests and energy chokepoints if Iran's infrastructure is threatened (Press TV); Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei said any escalation 'will undoubtedly bring about consequences' and 'our hands are not tied.' No retaliatory action reported in the window.

events.title: Beijing rejects the campaign; Chinese banks stay off the list
events.summary: China's Foreign Ministry said sanctions and pressure tactics do not help and Beijing would do what was necessary to protect its interests — its first formal response to Operation Economic Outcast. Madanizadeh claimed neither China nor Russia had 'accepted' the measures. Treasury's ~60 designations included no Chinese financial institutions; Reuters reports Washington is wary of hitting banks ahead of expected Trump–Xi talks next month.

events.title: Hegseth: 'by no means are we foreclosing using kinetic strikes anywhere in the Strait of Hormuz or around Iran'
events.summary: The defense secretary told reporters military options remain open against Iran despite the pivot to economic warfare — a counterpoint to the campaign's threat-only opening day. Pentagon messaging kept the blockade's enforcement backdrop visible as the tanker-strike report broke.

events.title: Munir wraps one-day Tehran mission without visible outcome
events.summary: Pakistan's army chief concluded the visit begun Monday after meeting Pezeshkian, Araghchi and other senior officials. Pezeshkian said Washington must 'correct its tone and approach… relying on coercion and bullying will only complicate the processes.' Three Pakistani sources said Trump initiated a call with Munir last week ahead of the trip, asking Islamabad to push Tehran back to negotiations. No breakthrough or next round announced.

events.title: Oil extends decline; dollar wobbles as markets price a threats-first rollout
events.summary: Brent hovered near $92 and WTI near $85 after falling more than 2% on Monday — prices fell despite the tanker strike, which traders read as noise rather than closure risk. The dollar struggled to hold gains as investors parsed the sanctions; NAB's Attrill flagged possible pre-sanction dollar hoarding. TotalEnergies' CEO put the cost of shipping a supertanker cargo through Hormuz at ~$20 million. Asian refiners nearly doubled September-loading US crude purchases to 40M+ barrels from 22M in August (Kpler/Vortexa/Sparta via Bloomberg).

events.title: Murphy: 'D-Day' is 'desperate window dressing… tragically, Iran won'
events.summary: Senator Chris Murphy called the sanctions a cover for military failure: Iran now controls the Strait it didn't control before the war, retains 30 of 33 missile sites along it, and 'we've already sanctioned basically everything in Iran we can.' The sharpest Democratic framing yet of the campaign, unaccompanied by any announced legislative response.

dossier: Night count: 26th consecutive without confirmed strikes inside Iran (the Ash Shishah tanker strike was maritime, off Oman — outside Iran). CENTCOM blockade accounting carried unchanged at 70 redirected / 3 disabled / 2 boarded; Crypto Briefing (Aug 24, citing centcom.mil) alone reports 71 diverted with 40+ humanitarian vessels passed through — centcom.mil blocked direct fetch (Akamai Access Denied), tally update unverified, watch next release. Timing caveat: UKMTO warning 120-26 issued late Monday US Eastern / early Tuesday Gulf local per NDTV and Mint ('early Tuesday local time') — treat as overnight straddling the UTC boundary; not captured in yesterday's report. Kpler weekly picture (via TWZ): Hormuz crossings +2.5% to 121, laden transits −27%, sanctioned crossings 9→16, use of Iran's unilateral routing scheme up to 46.3%; Bab al-Mandeb +3.1% to 269. SPR fell ~3.7M barrels to 289.7M last week, lowest since November 1982, under the 172M-barrel release agreement; Barchart: '41 days of crude oil inventory left'. Also caught up from Monday evening: State Dept component of Outcast sanctioned individuals/companies facilitating petroleum-petrochemical trade or supporting military action against US forces (JPost). Iranian citizens reportedly facing worsening fuel shortages and longer petrol queues (Bloomberg via CNBC TV18). Netanyahu told Channel 14 Iran tried to assassinate one of his sons — his claim, unverified, Israel track. Prediction market pricing ~5.5% YES on Hormuz traffic normalizing by Sep 30 (Crypto Briefing/Vera). From the ABC explainer: ICG's Rafati — China is the target that matters; ex-State's Eyre — 'we've done the low-hanging fruit… the tree'; Rafati warns Iran can still conduct 'counterpressure strikes' while guns are silent. Ghalibaf (X): no one buys America's bombast; trading partners don't take the statements into account. Tehran's stated conditions for reopening Hormuz: end the naval blockade, withdraw US forces, pay war reparations; separate talks with Oman on jointly managing the waterway regardless of a US deal (Mint). Reuters live blog for Aug 24 had expired entries by fetch time; core wire fetched directly instead.
